title: Add code-lang attribute to code element

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body: ### What problem are you trying to solve? In @edent's recent [blog post about the `code` element](https://shkspr.mobi/blog/2024/08/what-programming-language-is-in-this-code-block/) he mentions that there could be a gap in the HTML spec for defining the programming language of code in a code block. For example, I would like to mark up the following code snippet to show that it is Rust code: ```rust fn main() { println!("Hello World!"); } ``` The existing lang global attribute is not suitable for this, as it's supposed to be used for human languages, not programming. ### What solutions exist today? According to [the current HTML spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-code-element) > there is no formal way to indicate the language of computer code being marked up. But, > authors who wish to mark [code](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-code-element) elements with the language used, e.g. so that syntax highlighting scripts can use the right rules, can use the [class](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#classes) attribute, e.g. by adding a class prefixed with "language-" to the element. The problem with this is that naming classes with a "language-" prefix is not used by browsers, and as the spec mentions, it's mainly for the benefit of third party styling libraries. Schema.org has a microdata type for [SoftwareSourceCode](https://schema.org/SoftwareSourceCode), but this is overly verbose and again, not used by browsers (or styling libraries). ### How would you solve it? I would propose adding a 'code-lang' attribute to the code element, with this example syntax along similar lines suggested by @edent: ```html fn main() { println!("Hello World!"); } ``` The language codes could be standardised on the [pygments language short code list](https://pygments.org/languages/), or another standard coding language identifier? Language version would be specified with a semi colon. ### Anything else? Ideally this (might?) allow browsers to read programming languages in code blocks and add syntax highlighting to the default user agent stylesheet, but I recognise that's a very ambitious outcome for this proposal.
